christianOrgs.name: Columbia Catholic Ministry
christianOrgs.blurb: Students from Columbia College, Columbia Engineering, Barnard and General Studies who form a close-knit fellowship built around integrating the Catholic faith into daily life. Runs out of the Thomas Merton Institute on 114th Street with weekly Mass, student-led events and access to priests and missionaries.
christianOrgs.where: Thomas Merton Institute, 405 W 114th St, New York, NY 10025

christianOrgs.name: Columbia Christian Fellowship International (CCFI)
christianOrgs.blurb: A multilingual InterVarsity chapter for international students and scholars, built around reconciliation across ethnic, cultural and language backgrounds. Meets for Bible study, open discussion of faith questions and community service.
christianOrgs.where: Columbia University Irving Medical Center, and The Arbor in Riverdale

christianOrgs.name: Compass Christian Koinonia (CCK)
christianOrgs.blurb: An undergraduate fellowship connected to Compass Fellowship Church, meeting for weekly worship and small-group Bible study.

christianOrgs.name: InterVarsity Christian Fellowship (IVCF)
christianOrgs.blurb: The Morningside campus InterVarsity chapter — an interdenominational fellowship open to the whole campus community.

christianOrgs.name: Columbia SOON Movement
christianOrgs.blurb: A campus Christian fellowship listed among Columbia's recognized religious student organizations.

christianOrgsNote: Columbia Catholic Ministry and CCFI were confirmed on the pages linked above. The rest came from search results rather than a directory page we could open, so treat the names as a starting point and the missing contacts as genuinely missing — check Columbia Religious Life's student organizations list before reaching out. Columbia recognizes new groups only once a year, so this roster changes slowly.

startingAnRso.intro: Religious and spiritual groups at Columbia are recognized through the Student Governing Board (SGB), one of the boards advised by Undergraduate Student Life. Recognition happens once a year: in the 2026 cycle the application opened 2 February and closed 8 March, governing board interviews ran 1–12 April, decisions were announced 24 April, and newly recognized groups became official in September. The two-semester programming rule below is the part worth planning around — a new group is expected to run unofficially for a full year before it can apply.
requirements: A recommendation for recognition from an Undergraduate Student Life-advised governing board — for religious, spiritual, ideological or activist groups, that board is the Student Governing Board (SGB).
A mission statement distinct from any currently recognized student group, and a niche on campus that nothing else fills.
A student group constitution, in compliance with all University and USL policies.
An executive board made up of at least three-quarters undergraduates at CC, SEAS, Barnard or GS.
At least two semesters of active programming before SGB will consider the group for recognition.
Autonomy: the group's own members, not outside parties, must control its agenda and decisions.
Where a national organization's policies conflict with Columbia's rules or the SGB constitution, Columbia's rules take precedence.
Groups whose primary purpose is lobbying for legislation or campaigning for a candidate for public office are not eligible.
Apply through the USL New Group Recognition webform during the spring window.

startingAnRso.note: Requirements come from the Columbia College/Columbia Engineering recognition page and SGB's own criteria; the dates are the 2026 cycle. Confirm the current window before starting — it opens once a year, and missing it costs twelve months. Graduate and mixed-school groups apply to the Interschool Governing Board (IGB) instead, and Barnard-serving groups to GBB.
